lc_person: Michael Edward Brown, international-security scholar; author of Flying Blind and editor of International Security.
item_person: Michael E. Brown, political scientist affiliated with Georgetown and the Elliott School of International Affairs.

evidence.says: Flying Blind (1991) supplies the fuller name Michael Edward Brown and a data-sheet birth year of 1954. Rational Choice and Security Studies (2000) identifies him with Georgetown and as editor of International Security.

Political scientist with Georgetown and Elliott School affiliations; lists LC n91054852 and the exact key Open Library ID OL224165A. Its preferred birth year is 1959, imported from Wikipedia; another statement gives 1954, citing Czech and Israeli authority records.
Names Michael Edward Brown, political scientist, born 1954, with Georgetown and Elliott School affiliations.
Lists Ethnic Conflict and International Security, The International Dimensions of Internal Conflict, and other security studies books.
The Gender and Security Agenda (2020) names its editor Brown, Michael E. (Michael Edward), 1954-, matching the Open Library bibliography.

notes: Same scholar despite the year conflict. Prefer 1954 from LC’s author data sheet, corroborated by DNB; Open Library also carries 1959. Wikidata flags its VIAF identifier as a conflation.

lc_person: Oscar Zanetti Lecuona, historian; author of Caminos para el azúcar and Historia mínima de Cuba.
item_person: Oscar Zanetti, historian also named Óscar Adolfo Zanetti Lecuona, born 1946.

evidence.says: Caminos para el azúcar (1987) gives Oscar Zanetti Lecuona and birth year 1946. Historia mínima de Cuba (2013) uses Oscar Zanetti Lecuona on its title page and Oscar Zanetti on its cover; the flap identifies a historian born 1946.
Names Oscar Zanetti, gives the fuller name Óscar Adolfo Zanetti Lecuona, occupation historian and birth year 1946, and lists LC n91088158.

notes: LC directly documents the shortened name used by Wikidata. No independent key_evidence was supplied; the key name matches LC.

lc_person: Olga Maiorova, University of Michigan scholar of literature and history; author of From the Shadow of Empire.
item_person: Ol’ga Jevgen’jevna Majorova, literary historian, philologist and university teacher, born 1957.

evidence.says: Connects O. E. Maĭorova with Olga Maiorova at Michigan, author of From the Shadow of Empire (2010). The Dostoevsky in Context (2015) source supplies birth year 1957; the Kavelin source names O. E. Maĭorova as textual editor.
Labels the person Ol’ga Jevgen’jevna Majorova; gives literary historian, philologist, university teacher, birth year 1957, LC n91089780 and IdRef 07427273X.
Names Maïorova, Olga Evguenievna (1957-), with parallel form Majorova, Olʹga Evgenʹevna, and cites the same 1989 Kavelin edition as LC.
The supplied O. E. Maĭorova author record lists From the Shadow of Empire.
Identifies Olga Maiorova as associate professor of Slavic Languages and Literatures and lists From the Shadow of Empire (2010).

notes: Initials and different transliterations explain the name mismatch; the shared work and IdRef record resolve the identity.

lc_person: Rosamunde Neugebauer, art historian publishing also as Rosa von der Schulenburg; author of George Grosz.
item_person: Rosa von der Schulenburg, art historian, born 1958.

evidence.says: Cites Erlesen gestiftet (1991) under Rosamunde Neugebauer and George Grosz (1993) under Rosamunde Neugebauer Gräfin von der Schulenburg, with birth year 1958.
Names Rosa von der Schulenburg, art historian born 1958; lists GND 115668926 and LC n92072418.
Connects Rosa von der Schulenburg with the variant Rosamunde Neugebauer, art historian, birth year 1958, LC n92072418 and Wikidata Q95190716.
Lists George Grosz and Zeichnen im Exil, Zeichen des Exils? under Rosamunde Neugebauer.

notes: The institutional GND presentation explicitly connects both names. LC’s Carl Blechen/Rosa citation is marked notfound, so the verdict relies on its found George Grosz citation and the institutional authority record.

lc_person: Konstantin Viktorovich Pleshakov, political scientist and writer on Russian history; also publishes as Constantine Pleshakov.

evidence.says: Fizika (1992) expands the name to Konstantin Viktorovich Pleshakov. Inside the Kremlin’s Cold War (1996) uses Constantine Pleshakov. Krasnyĭ kamenʹ (2001) supplies birth year 1959 and identifies a political scientist writing history and novels.
Names Constantine Pleshakov, political scientist born 1959, with LC n93094240 and GND 113333692.
Lists Konstantin Viktorovich Pleshakov and Constantine Pleshakov as name forms, birth year 1959, political scientist and writer, with work on the Kremlin and international relations.
The supplied Konstantin Pleshakov author record lists Fizika and The Crimean Nexus, among other works.

notes: LC explicitly records Constantine as a publication name; this is a name-form mismatch.

lc_person: Oleg Vladimirovich Naumov, archivist born 1958; co-editor of Stalin’s Letters to Molotov, 1925–1936.
item_person: Oleg Georgievich Naumov, politician and member of the third State Duma, born 1953.

evidence.says: Stalin’s Letters to Molotov, 1925–1936 (1995) names Oleg V. Naumov. A 2015 citation to the Federal Archival Agency expands the name to Oleg Vladimirovich Naumov, gives birth year 1958 and identifies the former director of the archive of social-political history.

Describes a politician born 1953 and member of the third State Duma. Its Russian sitelink names Oleg Georgievich Naumov, and a Latvian identifier also specifies that patronymic and year. It nevertheless carries LC n94108746.
The key author Oleg V. Naumov lists Stalin’s Letters to Molotov, 1925–1936, Road to Terror and Yezhov, matching the LC archivist’s bibliography.

notes: Wrong Wikidata association: both patronymic and career differ. Birth year 1958 is supported here through LC’s institutional-source citation; the original agency page timed out. No replacement QID established in the brief search.

lc_person: Spyros A. Sofos, political scientist and co-editor of Nation and Identity in Contemporary Europe.
item_person: Spyros Sofos, political scientist linked to LC n95098691 and GND 137330057; Wikidata gives birth year 1944.

evidence.says: Nation and Identity in Contemporary Europe (1995 CIP) names Spyros A. Sofos and supplies birth year 1964 in the galley; the authorized heading is Sofos, Spyros A., 1964-.
Names Spyros Sofos, political scientist, with LC n95098691 and GND 137330057. Its 1944 birth statement cites BnF 134871106; another identifier names him Sofos, Spyros A., 1964-.
Names Sophos/Sofos, Spyros A., political scientist associated with Lund; gives birth year 1964.
Names Sofos, Spyros A. (1944-), political scientist at Portsmouth, and cites Nation and Identity in Contemporary Europe. Thus the 1944 disagreement exists in BnF as well as Wikidata.
Identifies Spyros Sofos as a humanities scholar of nationalism and politics, previously at Lund, and co-editor with Brian Jenkins of Nation and Identity in Contemporary Europe (1996).

notes: Prefer 1964 from LC’s galley citation, corroborated by DNB. BnF conflicts at 1944, but the identical work establishes the same person. No independent key_evidence was supplied; the key name matches LC.

Labels Moshe Helinger, alias Mosheh Helinger, political scientist and university teacher associated with Bar-Ilan; gives birth year 1960 and LC n95103837.
The key Moshe Hellinger record lists both Hagut medinit bi-yetsirot Dosṭoyevsḳi and Religious Zionism and the Settlement Project, matching LC.
